questions.topic: eGurukul · Metabolism in Fed, Fasting, Starvation & Diabetic States
questions.stem: The choice of metabolic fuel to meet body energy demand varies depending on availability. Which of the following is the preferred fuel for the body in a fasting state?
questions.solutionHtml:
Fats
  • The preferred fuel for the body in the Fasting state is mainly Fats.
  • Fats stored in adipose tissues are broken down into fatty acids which undergo oxidation to give energy during fasting and starvation.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 133-135

questions.topic: eGurukul · Metabolism in Fed, Fasting, Starvation & Diabetic States
questions.stem: Food products made of carbohydrates with low glycemic index help control blood sugar levels and are recommended for diabetics. Which of the following has the highest glycemic index?
questions.solutionHtml:
Galactose

Glycemic index (GI): It is a measure of the Increase in blood glucose after the test dose of carbohydrate compared with that of an equivalent amount of glucose.

  • Glucose and galactose have a glycemic index of 1 (or 100%), the same as maltose, isomaltose, lactose, and trehalose, which form these monosaccharides on hydrolysis.
  • GI is a value assigned to foods based on how slowly or how quickly those foods cause an increase in blood glucose levels.
  • Foods with low-GI values are the preferred choice as they are slowly digested and absorbed, causing a slower and smaller rise in blood sugar levels.
  • On the other hand, foods with a high GI value should be limited since they are quickly digested and absorbed, resulting in a rapid rise and fall in blood sugar levels

Low GI (≤55)

Fructose, beans, grains

Medium GI (56-69)

Table sugar or sucrose

High GI (≥70)

High fructose corn syrup, glucose, sweets, rice, maltose 1996

 




Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No. 366

questions.topic: eGurukul · Metabolism in Fed, Fasting, Starvation & Diabetic States
questions.stem: A key metabolite formed and utilized under fed and fasting states is acetyl-CoA. The major source of acetyl-CoA under a fed state is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Pyruvate
  • Acetyl-CoA is formed in the metabolism of carbohydrates, fats & proteins.
  • However, in the fed-state, the major source of fuel utilized is carbohydrates followed by fats and proteins. So, in the fed state major source of acetyl-CoA will be carbohydrates.
  • Carbohydrate gets broken down to Glucose which forms pyruvate & then acetyl CoA by glycolysis and link reaction respectively.
  • So the best answer here is Pyruvate.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 133-135

questions.stem: A 28 years old man suffering from intractable vomiting is presented to a hospital and was unable to eat or drink for the past 3 days. His blood analysis still shows a normal glucose level. Which of the following process is mainly responsible for the blood glucose maintenance in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Liver gluconeogenesis
  • As the patient has not taken any food for the past 3 days, he is in a starvation state. Glucagon released under starvation will cause the activation of gluconeogenic enzymes in the liver which will maintain the blood glucose needed for the functioning of vital organs such as the brain and heart and RBCs. So, the answer is liver gluconeogenesis.
  • The figure below shows the role of the liver in the fed and fasting state under hormonal control.
  • Fed state is mainly related to glycogen metabolism while fasted state shows a process related to gluconeogenesis from gluconeogenic substrates




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 142-145

questions.stem: When the body is devoid of any external source of food for 18 hours or longer, the main source of fuel utilized will be from:
questions.solutionHtml:
Adipose tissue
  • 18 hours or longer is considered a stage of fasting. There will be the release of glucagon which will activate hormone-sensitive lipase in the adipose tissue.
  • This enzyme will act on adipose TG reserves to release fatty acids that will travel to the liver via blood and form acetyl CoA by beta-oxidation. The acetyl-CoA has 3 different fates as shown in the attached Mantra:

questions.topic: eGurukul · Metabolism in Fed, Fasting, Starvation & Diabetic States
questions.stem: Which one of the following tissues can metabolize glucose, fatty acids, and ketone bodies for ATP production?
questions.solutionHtml:
Muscle
  • Muscles can use all three glucose, fatty acids & ketone bodies. It mainly uses glucose in the fed state, fatty acids in the fasting state and fatty acid and ketone bodies in starvation.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 627

questions.topic: eGurukul · Metabolism in Fed, Fasting, Starvation & Diabetic States
questions.stem: Ketone bodies are formed and utilized by various organs (brain, heart, etc) as the major sources of energy during fasting/starvation. The increase in the formation of ketone bodies during fasting is a result of:

options.label: B
options.text: Decrease in the formation of Acetyl CoA in the liver

options.label: C
options.text: Increased levels of free fatty acids in the blood

options.label: D
options.text: Inhibition of β-oxidation of fatty acids in the liver

questions.answerText: Increased levels of free fatty acids in the blood
questions.solutionHtml:
Increased levels of free fatty acids in the blood
  • In fasting, free fatty acids bound to albumin are increased due to increased activity of Hormone-sensitive lipase in adipose tissue as this enzyme breaks TG into glycerol & fatty acids.
  • These fatty acids are taken up by the liver.
  • β-oxidation of these fatty acids in the liver provides the acetyl CoA for ketogenesis.
  • Hepatic ketogenesis is also stimulated by elevated levels of glucagon during fasting.




Textbook of Medical Biochemistry by Dinesh Puri 3rd Edition Page No. 320-321

questions.stem: Respiratory quotient after heavy carbohydrate meal is:
questions.solutionHtml:
1.2

RQ (Respiratory quotient) =

For various macromolecules, RQ is different

  • If excess carbohydrate is taken then it is more than 1.
  • Heavy carbohydrate content when taken into the diet, carbohydrates will convert into fats.
  • Carbohydrates have more oxygen and fats have less oxygen, so when a more oxygen compound gets converted into less oxygen compound, oxygen is released which is used for oxidation, hence we require less O2 from outside for the metabolism of carbohydrate, RQ = = RQ will increase

questions.topic: eGurukul · Metabolism in Fed, Fasting, Starvation & Diabetic States
questions.stemHtml: Following are the test done for proteins, sugar & ketones. Which will be positive in the starvation state in urine?
questions.solutionHtml:
Only 3
  • The 3rd tube shows a positive Rothera’s test for the detection of ketone

Tests for detection of ketone bodies

  • Rothera’s test
    • The purple color ring at the junction of 2 liquids = Positive test
    • Given positive by Acetoacetate & Acetone
  • Gerhard’s test
    • Given positive by Acetoacetate only
  • Test for β-Hydroxy Butyrate – as this is the main ketone body found in the blood and urine of patients during ketoacidosis
    • No specific test available for β-Hydroxy Butyrate
    • So, in the sample, β-Hydroxy Butyrate is first oxidized to acetoacetate
    • Then we can perform Rothera’s or Gerhard’s test.
  • In Starvation, Excess of TG breakdown and acetyl CoA formation leads to an increase in ketone body formation which eventually starts coming in urine. So, urine will give a positive test for ketone bodies.




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 220

questions.topic: eGurukul · Metabolism in Fed, Fasting, Starvation & Diabetic States
questions.stem: Patient with Type I diabetes mellitus, with complaints of polyuria. Which of the following is commonly occurring in this state in his body?

options.label: C
options.text: Increased conversion of fatty acid to acetyl-CoA

questions.answerText: Increased conversion of fatty acid to acetyl-CoA
questions.solutionHtml:
Increased conversion of fatty acid to acetyl-CoA

Metabolic change in DM:

  • Ketoacidosis – due to an increase in plasma-free fatty acid. The low insulin condition will promote the activity of HSL to release FFA which undergoes β-oxidation in the liver to form acetyl-CoA
  • Hyperglycemia -It is primarily due to reduced glucose uptake by tissues and its increased production via gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis.



Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No. 338, 339

questions.topic: eGurukul · Metabolism in Fed, Fasting, Starvation & Diabetic States
questions.stem: The respiratory quotient (RQ) is a useful quantity to measure the energy expenditure of an organism to know certain metabolic states of the body. In Diabetes, What happens to RQ:

options.label: B
options.text: RQ increases & on giving Insulin it again decreases

options.label: C
options.text: RQ is not affected in Diabetes

options.label: D
options.text: RQ decreases & on giving Insulin it again increases

questions.answerText: RQ decreases & on giving Insulin it again increases
questions.solutionHtml:
RQ decreases & on giving Insulin it again increases
  • In a normal person in a fed state, the main fuel for the body is carbohydrates. But in a diabetic patient, the main fuel for the body is fats as carbohydrate/glucose is not entering the cells due to relative or absolute deficiency of insulin.
  • So, RQ decreases in Diabetes as the RQ of fats is less than the RQ for carbohydrates.
  • But on giving Insulin, RQ again rises as glucose starts entering cells through GLUT-4 and now cells will again start using glucose.



Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No. 359
